title: Mastering CSS Flexbox
subtitle: A Comprehensive Guide to Flexible Layouts

title: Flex Container
body:
A flex container is the parent element that establishes a flex context for its direct children.  By setting the `display: flex` property on an element, you transform it into a flex container, enabling its children to be arranged using flexbox properties. This provides powerful control over alignment and space distribution within the container.

Understanding the flex container is crucial, as it dictates how its children, known as flex items, will behave and interact with each other.

title: Container Setup
description: This code snippet demonstrates how to declare a flex container and set initial alignment properties.

title: Flex Items
body:
Flex items are the direct children of a flex container. They are automatically arranged according to the flexbox rules, and their size and position can be precisely controlled using flex properties. These items can be any valid HTML element, such as divs, paragraphs, or images.

Items inherit their flex behavior from the container, but you can further customize each item individually to achieve complex layouts.

title: Main Axis
body:
The main axis is the primary direction in which flex items are laid out within a flex container. By default, the main axis is horizontal, running from left to right. However, you can change this direction using the `flex-direction` property to create vertical or other directional layouts.

Understanding the main axis is vital for controlling the alignment and ordering of flex items within the container.

title: Flex Wrap
body:
The `flex-wrap` property controls whether flex items should wrap onto multiple lines if they exceed the container's size.  By default, items are arranged in a single line, potentially overflowing the container. Setting `flex-wrap: wrap` allows items to wrap to the next line when needed, creating a multi-row layout.

This is especially useful when dealing with content of varying lengths or when you want to ensure items don't become too narrow.

description: This example demonstrates how to enable flex item wrapping using `flex-wrap: wrap;`

title: Align Items
body:
The `align-items` property controls the alignment of flex items along the cross axis, which is perpendicular to the main axis. It determines how items are positioned vertically when the main axis is horizontal, or horizontally when the main axis is vertical. Common values include `stretch`, `flex-start`, `flex-end`, and `center`.

Proper alignment ensures a visually appealing and well-structured layout, regardless of the content's size.

title: Vertical Alignment
description: This example shows how to vertically align flex items using `align-items: center;`

title: Justify Content
body:
The `justify-content` property controls the alignment of flex items along the main axis. It determines how items are distributed horizontally when the main axis is horizontal, or vertically when the main axis is vertical. Options include `flex-start`, `flex-end`, `center`, `space-between`, and `space-around`.

Using `justify-content` allows for precise control over the spacing and positioning of items within the container.

title: Horizontal Spacing
description: This example uses `justify-content: space-between;` to create horizontal spacing between flex items.

title: Summary
bullets: Flex wrap enables items to move to the next line.
Align items control vertical (or horizontal) positioning.
Justify content distributes items along the main axis.

title: Order Property
body:
The `order` property allows you to change the visual order of flex items without modifying the HTML source code. Items with lower order values appear earlier in the layout. The default order value is 0, so you can use negative values to move items to the beginning or higher values to move them to the end.

This is extremely useful for responsive design, allowing you to rearrange content based on screen size.

title: Reordering Items
description: This code demonstrates how to reorder flex items using the `order` property.

title: Flex Basis
body:
The `flex-basis` property specifies the initial main size of a flex item. It determines how much space the item should occupy before any available space is distributed according to the `flex-grow` and `flex-shrink` properties. If `flex-basis` is set to `auto`, the item's size will be determined by its content.

This allows you to define a base size for your items, which can then be adjusted based on the available space.

title: Setting Item Size
description: This example demonstrates how to set the initial size of flex items using `flex-basis: 200px;`

title: Flex Grow/Shrink
body:
The `flex-grow` property defines how much a flex item should grow relative to other flex items in the container. The `flex-shrink` property defines how much a flex item should shrink relative to other flex items. These properties are used to distribute available space or accommodate content overflow.

Combining these with `flex-basis` provides granular control over item sizing and responsiveness.

title: Dynamic Item Sizing
description: This code uses `flex-grow: 1;` and `flex-shrink: 1;` to allow flex items to dynamically resize.

title: Summary
bullets: The order property allows for reordering without HTML changes.
Flex basis sets the initial size of items.
Flex grow and shrink control dynamic resizing.
